newsitem.title: USA: Reading & Bates, Falcon in $5 billion merger.
newsitem.headline: Reading & Bates, Falcon in $5 billion merger.

text.p: Falcon Drilling Co. and Reading & Bates Corp., riding a rising tide of offshore oil and gas exploration, are merging in a $5 billion deal that will form the world's largest offshore drilling fleet.

The combined company, to be renamed R&B Falcon Corp., will operate in the booming coastal and deepwater oil and gas production zones, with 14 vessels capable of drilling in greater than 3,000 feet of water and 25 jack-up rigs for shallow waters.

The deal, announced late Thursday night, lifted shares of the two Houston-based companies Friday. Reading & Bates gained $3.31 to $33.625 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange, after moving up 10 percent Thursday. Falcon edged up 87.5 cents to $58.75, also on the NYSE.

The deal continues a wave of consolidation sweeping the offshore drilling industry as rising demand for drilling equipment pushes up daily rates for a rig and its operating crew, and forces oil and gas producers into longer-term contracts.
"I think this gives us a pretty good platform to both grow internally as well as to look at different opportunities," Reading & Bates Chairman Paul Loyd said.

Reading & Bates has been positioning for the surge in deepwater Gulf of Mexico drilling, contracting with partner Conoco in June for construction of a second drillship capable of operating in waters as deep as 10,000 feet.
Falcon nearly doubled its revenues in the first quarter of this year compared with last year and is converting three salvage ships into drillships to expand its deepwater operations.

"Both earnings and cash flow should be accretive really from day one, without really taking into account a lot of synergies, which I think we both feel will be significant over the next couple of years," Falcon Chairman Steven Webster said.
Stocks in offshore drilling companies have rallied this year, largely on stepped-up exploration spending in the Gulf of Mexico that is fuelling forecasts of rising rates for offshore equipment.
With the merger, R&B Falcon joins Transocean Offshore Inc. and Diamond Offshore Drilling Inc. as the three dominant deepwater drilling companies, analysts said.

"The bigger companies are going to be generating huge amounts of free cash," Simmons & Co. analyst Dan Pickering said. "Bigger is better, particularly in terms of the ability to train people and bring on crews."
Loyd will become chairman of the new company and Webster was named R&B Falcon's president and CEO.
Falcon shareholders will receive one R&B Falcon common share for each their common shares, while Reading & Bates shareholders will get 0.59 share in the new company for each of their shares.
The deal, which must be approved by shareholders of both companies, is slated to close in the fourth quarter. The new company's board will include five directors from each company.
